description: Jhalana Leopard Reserve sits inside Jaipur city, in the Aravalli hills, just 8–12 km from the old city. Guests explore the reserve in an open 4x4 Gypsy with a forest-department driver. Beyond leopards, the reserve supports striped hyena, desert fox, golden jackal, nilgai and more than 200 bird species, including Indian eagle-owl and crested serpent eagle. description: Architecture Walk in Jaipur – Explore the Planned City’s Hidden Architectural Wonders Jaipur is famous for its grand forts and palaces, but the real beauty of the city lies in its architecture and urban planning. Built in the 18th century, Jaipur is one of India’s earliest planned cities, designed using principles of Vastu Shastra, geometry, and scientific urban planning. The city was planned with wide streets, organized markets, residential zones, and public spaces, creating a city that was both beautiful and functional. This Architecture Walk is designed for travelers who want to look beyond monuments and understand the design, planning, and architectural details of the old city. During the walk, you will explore traditional havelis, hidden courtyards, ancient streets, and architectural elements that show how Jaipur was designed to suit climate, lifestyle, and culture. This experience helps you see Jaipur not just as a historic city, but as a living example of intelligent urban design. Experience Highlights: Understand Jaipur’s grid-based city planning Learn about Vastu Shastra and urban design principles Explore traditional Rajasthani havelis Observe jharokhas, courtyards, and carved facades Learn about climate-responsive architecture Discover hidden architectural details in old streets Walk with a licensed architect guide
